title: Automated Inventory Reconciliation Workflow
business: Retail companies managing distributed warehouse systems across multiple cloud-native microservices.
problem: Manual reconciliation of inventory levels between disparate warehouse management APIs often leads to data inconsistency, high latency, and significant operational overhead when services fail to synchronize.
solution: Google Cloud Workflows orchestrates the interaction between independent HTTP-based warehouse APIs, managing retries, error handling, and sequential execution logic without requiring custom middleware infrastructure.
steps: Define the workflow sequence to query the primary warehouse API for stock levels.
Implement conditional logic to verify if the response indicates a successful data retrieval.
Invoke secondary service endpoints to update inventory records based on the primary data.
Configure automated retry policies for transient HTTP failures to ensure service resilience.
Log execution status to monitor the reconciliation process completion.
outcome: Improved data integrity across inventory systems and reduced manual intervention for routine synchronization tasks.
limitation: Workflows are designed for orchestration, not high-throughput data processing; checking execution history in the console is the primary method to identify bottlenecks in long-running sequences.
